meta.signal: WS2812 NZR 800 kbps from RP2040 PIO (T0H~350ns, T1H~700ns, bit 1.25us, exact crystal-derived timing)
meta.byte_layout: bit7=BS0 of PREVIOUS iteration, bit6=BS1 of PREVIOUS iteration, bit5..bit0=R0..R5 of THIS iteration. Chronological order within iteration i: R0..R5 at 37*i+[1,5,9,13,17,21], BS0 at 37*i+27, BS1 at 37*i+32 (stored in byte i+1 bits 7,6). First byte's bits 7..6 are garbage; the last iteration's BS0/BS1 are lost.
meta.trigger: capture starts at the first rising edge on the signal; sample R0 of iteration 0 lands ~1 cycle after the edge test fell through
meta.checksum: sum of 640 raw capture bytes mod 256
meta.payload_layout: DATA(16) || CRC8 || CRC8 || CRC8 || CRC8 = 20 bytes; frame = 4 + 20 + 4 = 28 bytes
meta.crc8: CRC-8/SMBUS (poly 0x07, init 0x00, no reflection, no xorout) over the DATA bytes only
meta.check_block: the same CRC8 repeated 4 times; the receiver's chase reference is the UNIQUE value holding >= 2 of the 4 votes, so one corrupted check byte is harmless and two differently-corrupted ones still leave a majority. A 2-2 tie or a full split (no such value) -> rank the distinct candidates by decode confidence and try in order.
meta.production_sizing: 48 data bytes + 4 check bytes = 52-byte payload, 60-byte frame = exactly 20 WS2812 LEDs (no pad byte; any surplus wire byte inflates the clock fit ~1.6%/byte -- bench/pad_law.py)
meta.delivery: single transmission: each logical frame goes on the wire exactly once; no repeats, no retries, no acks, no sequence numbers. The --reps captures in this dataset are independent bench acquisitions of the same frame, not protocol repeats.
